messages:
maria: Heads up — since ~03:00 UTC we've seen a spike in GPU pod evictions in eu-west1. ~120 evictions in the last hour, mostly from inference-worker-* pods. infra-bot: alert: eu-west1 gpu-eviction-rate > 100/hr. node-group: g4dn-inference-eu-west1. maria: eviction reason shows Killed for OOM and also 'NodePressure' in some cases. aj: NodePressure makes me think either memory pressure on node or kubelet eviction due to disk or kernel memory. can you paste `kubectl describe node` for one of the nodes? maria: pasted output below.

maria: ```
Name: gpu-eu-01
Taints: dedicated=inference:NoSchedule
Allocated resources:
  (total resources may be overcommitted)
  cpu: 48
  memory: 372Gi
  pods: 110
Events:
  Type    Reason     Age   From     Message
  ----    ------     ----  ----     -------
  Warning Evicted    10m   kubelet  The node was low on resource: ephemeral-storage
  Warning Evicted    9m    kubelet  The node was low on resource: memory
```

sanjay: ephemeral-storage evictions on GPU nodes? we've seen image pull cache filling up if model downloads are big. are we using ephemeral model caches on local SSDs? maria: yes, inference-worker downloads model shards to /var/lib/models/cache by design. ella: that cache should be size-limited by the init container but looks like it's not enforced on these nodes. aj: also seeing pods with `podPriority: 0` (BestEffort/Default) running alongside guaranteed workloads — scheduling mix might push eviction victims to the default pods, but NodePressure evicts based on kubelet scoring. vinh: I wonder if the autoscaler is adding nodes in the same AZ repeatedly which fragments GPU slots across AZs so we can't pack with binpacking. infra-bot: autoscaler: scaled up 3 nodes in eu-west1-azc, scaled down 1 in azb last 30m. maria: logs show scheduler had trouble finding contiguous GPUs for gang-scheduled jobs -> some pods pending then scheduled as singletons on different nodes which increases per-node memory footprint.

aj: this is a classic fragmentation + local cache problem. high pod churn + model downloads -> ephemeral-storage thrash -> NodePressure -> evictions. two-pronged approach: 1) limit cache size per node or use shared remote cache. 2) improve packing so model-serving pods colocate to fewer nodes (reduce replication of model caches). ella: agree, packing change could be `PodTopologySpread` + `requiredDuringScheduling` anti-affinity tweaks, or use `nodeAffinity` to prefer dedicated inference pool nodes with bigger SSDs. sanjay: also consider taint+toleration combos: move lower priority jobs off GPU pool by adding a soft taint and forcing non-critical pods to other groups.

maria: temporary mitigation: I've applied a DiskPressure eviction soft limit by bumping kubelet eviction thresholds on the GPU node pool, and set the model cache size env var to 8Gi for the worker. aj: careful — raising eviction threshold buys time but risks node instability. we need an automated flush of old caches. vinh: can we add a cronjob on the pool to `du -sh /var/lib/models/cache/*` and evict oldest when > X? infra-bot: job created: cache-cleaner-eu-west1 (CronJob) — runs every 15m in kube-system.

sanjay: long term we should reduce fragmentation: proposal: create a compacting binpacker policy for inference pool. algorithm: prefer nodes with existing model image layers and GPUs free rather than scattering. team: any constraints? ella: risk — could cause AZ imbalance. we have AZ spread quotas from infra compliance that require minimal cross-AZ redundancy for core services. aj: we can do soft-preference packing per AZ first, then cross-AZ if needed. also need to respect pod anti-affinity for fault domains.

maria: cost side: currently we spin up spot VMs for extra capacity which are getting preempted and add churn. maybe reserve 10% baseline reserved capacity for inference to reduce churn. vinh: reserved capacity = $$, but reduces eviction churn, might lower overall token cost because fewer model re-downloads. infra-bot: cost-estimate: 10% reserved on inference pool adds ~£6k/month.

ella: action items: 1) maria/aj implement cache-size env limit and cronjob (done). 2) sanjay draft compacting scheduler proposal + cost tradeoffs (sanjay). 3) vinh evaluate 10% reserved capacity and ROI. 4) infra runbook update for NodePressure on GPU nodes (maria).

aj: small test: add a scheduling predicate to prefer nodes with model-shard label `model-cache/has=<model-name>` and measure eviction rate. if >30% reduction we can roll to canary. maria: running canary now against inference-canary namespace. infra-bot: canary deployment: inference-canary/worker-v2 scaled to 12 across eu-west1.

vinh: FYI, network team flagged intermittent NIC resets in eu-west1-azc earlier today; could exacerbate image pulls and increase disk pressure due to repeated retries. I'm opening a ticket with cloud provider. maria: noted — will correlate timestamps with eviction spikes. aj: any objections to gradually lowering default pod parallel downloads from 4->1 to reduce concurrent disk stress? ella: sounds safe for now for downloads at startup.

maria: thanks all — will update after canary runs for 2 hours. aj: thanks, ping me if evictions resume. infra-bot: alert resolved: eviction-rate dropped below 30/hr. maria: :thumbsup:
